title: DDI assessment
text: May-2024, ICH published new harmonized guidance assessment enzyme- transporter-mediated drug interactions adopted ICH-abiding regulatory agencies, including FDA, EMA PMDA. Currently (Nov-2024), following guidance documents provided individual regulatory authorities: M12 Drug Interaction Studies (FDA, Aug-2024) M12 Questions Answers document (Aug-2024) ICH M12 Drug Interaction Studies (EMA, May-2024)

title: DDI assessment
text: general concept, risk enzyme transporter interactions evaluated given drug exposure level corresponds maximal unbound clinical exposure relevant pharmacokinetic compartment. interactions hepatic enzymes, unbound maximal plasma concentration steady state (\(I_{max,ss,u}\)) considered, intestinal enzymes victim orally administered drugs, maximal clinical dose, dissolved volume 250 mg (\(I_{gut}\)). interactions basolateral hepatic transporters (OATP1B1, OATP1B3), unbound hepatic inlet concentration (\(I_{max,inlet,u}\)) considered composed \(I_{max,ss,u}\) portal venous term reflecting intestinally absorbed drug escaping gut metabolism. concentrations can automatically derived following set drug-specific parameters: specification key compound parameters therefore first step formal analysis. scope package, key parameters aggregated ‘perpetrator’ object. package contains sample perpetrator object ficitional drug ‘examplinib’: ddir package provides multiple options create perpetrator objects. simplest case, function make_perpetrator() can used: options presented dedicated vignette (see vignette("load-data")). facilitate generation R notebook-based reports, property_table() can used print markdown-formatted table key compound parameters: Perpetrator compound parameters examplinib

title: Key perpetrator concentrations — kc,perpetrator-method
text: orally administered (parent) compounds, hepatic inlet concentration systemic concentration plus portal term: $$portal\ term = D*\frac{F_a*F_g*k_a}{Q_h*R_B}*1000\ ng/ml$$ \(D\) administered dose mg, \(F_a\) fraction absorbed oral administration, \(F_g\) fraction available gut metabolism, \(k_a\) absorption rate, \(Q_h\) hepatic blood flow \(R_B\) blood--plasma ratio. relevant hepatic inlet concentration (\(I_{max,inlet,u}\), also called \(I_h\) mechanistic static modeling equations) concentration sum maximal systemic plasma concentration portal contribution: $$I_{max,inlet,u}=(I_{max,ss} + portal\ term) * f_u$$

title: Key perpetrator concentrations — kc,perpetrator-method
text: orally administered (parent) compounds, villous concentration gut (\(I_{enteric}\), also called \(I_g\) mechanistic static modeling equations) calculated : $$I_{enteric,u} = D * \frac{F_a*k_a}{Q_{ent}} *1000\ ng/ml$$ \(F_a\) fraction absorbed oral administration, \(k_a\) absorption rate, \(Q_{ent}\) enteric villous blood flow \(R_B\) blood--plasma distribution ratio compound. Note per FDA guideline (refer FDA, 2020, Fig. 7, Rostami-Hodjegan Tucker, 2004) blood--plasma ratio plasma binding drug applicable.
